RED FIRST, PROVEN: wrote scaffold.test.tsx before either module existed and ran it — "Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests no tests", failing in Vite's transform on the missing ./fixtures.js and ./kernel.js specifiers. Then implemented to green.

THE TEST FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN CODE, and the fix went into production, not the test. First green run failed: "expected 36 to be 12". I had named the wrapper `cr.fact.<id>` and its inner spans `cr.fact.label` / `cr.fact.value`, so the spec's own audit selector `[data-testid^='cr.fact.']` matched 3 elements per fact instead of 1. That is worse than a wrong count: the spec §12 bar is "every cr.fact.* element has a cr.chip.* descendant", and every downstream surface task will write that selector. Under the old naming, label and value spans would have been counted as fact claims and — being chip-less — the audit would have failed for the wrong reason, or if written as a find-first, passed without ever inspecting a claim. Renamed the inner parts to `cr.label` / `cr.value`, reserving the `cr.fact.` prefix for wrappers alone, documented it in the Fact docblock, and added a pinning assertion that one Fact yields exactly one `cr.fact.*` element. Five surface tasks inherit this.

HONESTY SEAM (the named mapping decision), implemented and red-teamed both directions: presentTruthClass(input) distinguishes three origins where the kernel offers two. ABSENT (undefined/null) -> UNKNOWN descriptor + "class missing from payload" per spec §3.3. INVALID (present but unsupported) -> UNKNOWN descriptor + a note carrying the stable TRUTH_CLASS_INVALID code. PRESENT -> the kernel's descriptor, empty note. Both failure paths render UNKNOWN so nothing is ever defaulted upward, but they never look alike to an operator or a test. Hostile inputs asserted: {truthClass:"DAEMON_VERIFIED"}, "daemon_verified", "DAEMON_VERIFIED " (trailing space), "", 0, false, ["HUMAN_APPROVED"] — all INVALID, all high-contrast magenta. The truth mapping itself is never reimplemented: the UNKNOWN descriptor is obtained from describeTruthClass("UNKNOWN") behind a guard that throws if the kernel ever stops describing it, so a kernel contract change fails loudly instead of silently degrading the shell.

TRIPLE ENCODING: chip is a <button> carrying text (shortLabel), icon (glyph), colour (data-tone = semanticTone), plus data-border, data-origin, data-provenance-note, data-truth-class, aria-label, chipTestId, and a 24px min hit target. Tests assert the three channels independently, prove all five classes are distinguishable by glyph AND label alone (set size 5 each — the forced-monochrome bar), prove UNKNOWN is the only dashed border, and prove the chip is focusable, Enter/click-activatable, and advertises "press Enter for provenance.".

DoD-vs-SPEC DIVERGENCE — QA PLEASE READ, I did not silently pick a side. DoD 2 says "disconnected/stale fixtures disable mutation". The approved plan resolved this as a spec-verified BLOCKER: CR-LAG-001 requires stale display to be LABELLED with "commands not blocked by UI", so treating lag as a disable would be a UI-invented refusal. I satisfied both by modelling FOUR states instead of the planned three, and the extra one is not an invention — it is daemon-sourced. CONNECTED: affordances, mutations on. LAGGING: same affordances, mutations on, statusLabel names the staleness. DISCONNECTED: EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS, mutations off, banner text. HISTORICAL: built from contracts' own historicalRuntimeResult(), which returns empty affordances with requiresAffordanceRefresh true — that is the daemon's own "a replayed view carries no current authority" rule, and it is the genuine "stale disables mutation" case DoD 2 asks for. Crucially mutationsEnabled is DERIVED, never authored: connection !== "DISCONNECTED" && !requiresAffordanceRefresh && nextAllowedCommands.length > 0. A fixture author cannot hand-write an enabled action, and the test recomputes the rule for every snapshot rather than asserting four hardcoded booleans.

FIXTURES: six surfaces (goals, board, node, approval, evidence, doctor), 12 facts, each with a full §3.2 provenance record (event sequence + id, actor, session, lease epoch, ISO timestamp, typed link kind + ref). Two facts carry deliberately dishonest payloads — board.readiness omits its class entirely, doctor.relay supplies {class:"OBSERVED"} — so the ABSENT and INVALID paths are exercised by shipped fixture data, not only by test-only inputs. Marked CONTROL_ROOM_FIXTURE_KIND = "DEVELOPMENT_ONLY/NOT_CONFIRMATORY". Determinism is structural: no clock, no random, every value a literal; buildControlRoomFixtures() is JSON-identical across calls and the result is frozen. The connected affordance set goes through @moe/contracts buildNextAllowedCommands with a closed NODE_RUN/WORK_R
